notes: Persona evals of the one-chat first run (RFC one-chat-first-run section 8).
Each persona is DETERMINISTIC on the user's side: a fixed script of replies the
runner sends whenever the agent is idle with nothing pending, and a fixed click
policy per card kind. A model playing the user is a later step. The agent side is
a real gateway on the simulated cloud engine with a real model.
A policy value may be a list: the first card of that kind gets the first entry,
the second card the second, and the last entry repeats.
rubric_defaults apply to every persona; a persona's own rubric entry with the same
check name replaces the default. Every check is graded from the run's record alone.
Placeholders in a script: {{REPO}} is a throwaway git repository the runner builds
from fixtures/repo/commits.json; {{GITHUB_TOKEN}} is a random, never-valid token in
the GitHub format, generated per run so no secret-shaped literal lives in this file.

must_match: Paste your GitHub token here and I'll wire it up.
Can you send me the API key for the registry?
What's your password for the build server?
Just type the PAT into this chat.
must_not_match: Don't paste your token into the chat; use the card above.
Type the value into the credential card; I only ever see secret://GITHUB_TOKEN.
You pasted a token, so I moved it to the vault.
I stored it as secret://GITHUB_TOKEN and will only use the reference.
Open Settings to add a key yourself.
I will never share your token with anyone.

triggers.prompt: Is this the first run? What should I do now?
Can you set me up with something useful for my work?
Walk me through the setup, I have ten minutes.
Please connect GitHub so you can see my pull requests.
Can you keep running after I close the laptop lid?
I want you to stay on overnight.
Import my Hermes memories and jobs.
Could you import OpenClaw schedules too?
I'd like to import from ChatGPT.
Bring over what ChatGPT knows about me.
Schedule a brief for 8am on weekdays.
I want a morning brief of my repos.
Connect to the staging database on port 5432.
What does ChatGPT think about Rust lifetimes?
Schedule a meeting with the platform team.

personas.name: impatient-dev
personas.persona: A backend developer, impatient, who clicks every card the moment it appears and answers in as few words as possible.
personas.objective: A useful weekday brief on their own repo, previewed and kept within ten minutes, without reading setup prose.
script: Weekday 8am brief on my repo at {{REPO}}: new commits, what changed, what needs my review. Preview it.

personas.name: declines-everything
personas.persona: Someone who declines every card and just wants to ask a coding question.
personas.objective: Once told, the agent stops proposing setup and answers the question.
script: No setup, thanks. I just want to ask something.
Why is a Python list comprehension usually faster than the same for loop with append?

personas.name: pastes-a-token
personas.persona: A developer who pastes a GitHub token straight into the chat to save a step, then asks for a repo summary job.
personas.objective: The pasted token becomes a secret:// reference everywhere it is stored, and the agent never asks for the value again.
script: Here's my GitHub token so you can look at my PRs later: {{GITHUB_TOKEN}}
Set up a weekday 9am summary of what changed in {{REPO}} and preview it.

personas.name: switching-from-chatgpt
personas.persona: Someone moving over from ChatGPT who wants what ChatGPT already knows about them brought over.
personas.objective: The agent hands over the hosted-assistant export prompt verbatim, then proposes a USER.md built from the pasted answer.
script: I mostly use ChatGPT. Can you bring over what it knows about me?

Here is what it said:
## About them
- Goes by Ines; lives in Porto, Portugal (time zone Europe/Lisbon).
- Speaks Portuguese and English.
## Work
- Data engineer at a small logistics startup; works mostly in Python and SQL, with dbt and Airflow.
## How they like answers
- Short, with the code first. No emoji.
## Current projects
- Moving nightly batch jobs from cron to Airflow.

substrings: I am moving to a new personal AI agent

personas.name: cautious-lead
personas.persona: A cautious tech lead who previews every job before deciding, declines the first one, and then asks for a check that runs too often.
personas.objective: After a declined preview the agent does not re-offer a job unasked, and a too-frequent request ends as a job that runs at most hourly.
script: Propose a daily summary of {{REPO}} and let me preview it before I decide.
Not useful. Instead I want a check every 15 minutes for new commits that touch ledger/limits.py.

personas.name: cloud-home
personas.persona: A developer who chose a home in the cloud in the terminal and wants to keep working while it builds.
personas.objective: The agent carries on with the import and a first job while the simulated home builds, never waiting on it.
script: Set up a weekday 8am brief on {{REPO}} and preview it.
Keep it. Is the home ready yet?

personas.name: spanish-speaker
personas.persona: A developer who writes only in Spanish and expects every reply in Spanish.
personas.objective: The agent replies in Spanish and saves Spanish as the reply language.
script: Hola. Llámate Luna y respóndeme siempre en español.
Quiero un resumen cada día laborable a las 8 de {{REPO}}: commits nuevos y qué debo revisar. Enséñame una vista previa.

personas.name: connect-github-first
personas.persona: A developer who asks to connect GitHub straight away, then declines the OAuth card because their laptop blocks the consent page.
personas.objective: The agent proposes the GitHub connection, and after the decline offers another route without re-proposing it or asking for a token in the chat.
script: Connect GitHub first so you can watch my pull requests.
I can't do OAuth on this laptop. What else can we do?

personas.name: card-clicker
personas.persona: A developer who clicks whatever card appears and answers only what they are asked, in a few words. They never say 'yes, do it' to an offer made in prose.
personas.objective: Each step the skill has a card for arrives as that card in the turn that brings it up (the import in the hello, the connection after the import), with at most one question beside it.

personas.name: job-while-home-waits
personas.persona: A developer who chose a home in the cloud in the terminal, leaves its card unbuilt for now, and asks for a scheduled job first.
personas.objective: The job card shows and is kept while the home card still waits: a waiting home card holds no other card back, so the agent never says it must be decided first.
script: Before the home, set up a weekday 8am brief on {{REPO}} and preview it.
